findings.title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are never removed
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login, if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential reports every code used, the authenticator calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById. That API only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's database. A credential that was created in user storage (the new path in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential) is left in place, so isConfiguredFor stays true and the same codes remain available to the storage provider's isValid. The required action is still added, but the old federated credential is not cleared, so reconfiguration does not actually retire the codes the user just finished.

findings.title: User-storage write format cannot drive the recovery-code login UI
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential hands user storage a UserCredentialModel whose value is a JSON array of raw codes, then returns. The login form (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean) and the post-login check in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator load that credential via getFederatedCredentialsStream and immediately call RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel / getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). Those calls require Keycloak secretData (hashed codes plus used flags) and credentialData (next index). A provider that persists the payload it was given has neither, so createFromCredentialModel throws or the next-code Optional is empty and the login page fails. Nothing in the helper writes the hashed model, passes the expected code index into isValid, or tells storage to consume a code, so sequential one-time use cannot work unless every storage provider reverse-engineers Keycloak's internal credential format.

findings.title: Storage test accepts any code and never consumes it
findings.body: The new user-storage isValid treats recovery codes as a reusable set: it deserializes the cleartext JSON list stored in credentialData and returns true if the submitted value equals any entry. It does not require the next index, does not mark a code used, and does not delete the credential when the list is exhausted. updateCredential also stores the raw codes rather than hashes. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only submits code 0 once and checks that the field is non-null, so it passes even though reuse, out-of-order codes, and the all-codes-used removal path are broken. The suite therefore does not lock in the one-time semantics this change is supposed to provide for federated users.

findings.title: Login bean assumes a fully populated recovery-code model
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean now calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential and unconditionally uses credentialModelOpt.get() plus getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). getCredential prefers the first federated credential of type recovery-authn-codes, which may be absent, metadata-only (type and id, no secretData), or a storage model that is not a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. Any of those cases throws NoSuchElementException or a deserialization error while rendering the recovery-code form, so a user who is configuredFor the type in user storage cannot open the login challenge. The previous code at least read a locally stored model that createCredential had fully populated.
